reasons: In A the turns are short and each one reacts to the previous speaker. Benjamin's Day 1 Seer claim moves the talk at once: Kenji says 'No way', Minako asks if he is claiming Seer, Mizuki weighs whether he could be the wolf lying, and they converge on a vote. B's Day 0 is a long run of ceremonial padding: everyone paraphrases the last speaker about the Possessed and the Seer, then says formal goodnights ('As we conclude the first day', 'A delightful opening act'). B's Day 1 does build real friction when Mizuki goes after Benjamin, but it is buried under stock lines. Overall A's pace reads more like people talking, even though it is thin in places ('Kindness is good, but...').

The two are structurally almost identical. In B, Round 3 has Victoria raise a real catch about B (the hall being out of service during conversion) and keep it as a condition when she agrees. George stays consistent with his staffing concern, says 'I still lean toward A', and then votes A. In A everyone, George included ('I will concede to the group'), folds into a quick unanimous 'Agreed', which feels hurried and flattened. A's Round 1 is just a task list with no conversation. B's opening discussion of priorities before splitting the tasks is a little more like people orienting themselves.

A's Round 1 falls into a mechanical loop: all five say 'I'll stick with my choices' / 'I am ready' three times over, which no real group does. B's Round 1 has real back-and-forth on priorities. Rin teases the others ('You're all being so serious!') and Misaki pushes back ('Excitement is fine, but we can't ignore the numbers'). In B's Round 2, Ryuji and Shizue clash ('Kindness is a goal, but it cannot override practicality'), and Rin's 'I'm tired of all this talking about paperwork!' reads naturally. B ends in a real 3–2 split with Mio staying consistent on fairness. In A, Mio's final line ('I can't let the budget fail again... I'll take the risk and vote for Option C') contradicts itself.

A's Round 3 is real deliberation. Asuka warns that the narrow frontages may make rotation impractical, Midori fears 'arguing about whose driveway is in the way', and Shunichi answers Midori directly ('That's a fair point, Midori, but...'). May weighs rotation against standing at the bins at 7:40, and the group works through the trade-off before settling. In B the group agrees on rotation already by the end of Round 2. Round 3 then becomes three passes of near-identical endorsements ending in Rin's 'B! B! B!', so nobody is working anything out. B's Round 1 also has filler like Asuka's meta remark 'Let us proceed to the information gathering phase'.

These are close. A is tighter, but its Round 3 collapses into five bare 'C.' lines, and Yumi switches to Fixed Desks on a fresh rationale without much tension. In B, Yumi stays herself across rounds: she pushes back in Round 2 ('we're focusing so much on the downsides of moving that we're forgetting...'), voices doubt in Round 3, and then concedes reluctantly ('I still think we're missing out on the social side, but...'). That reads like a real person being persuaded. B also has explicit uptake ('I'm with Mizuki'), though its closing votes are formulaic too.

In A's Day 0 all five go round three times saying more or less the same thing about watching each other and the Possessed, and every line is padded out to full length (Benjamin's 'double-edged sword', Shizue's 'kind and open heart'). Day 1 of A does build a real thread (Minako presses Benjamin, Mizuki pushes, Kenji objects), but the speeches still sound like set pieces. In B, Benjamin's Day 1 Seer claim against Shizue gives the talk a real turning point that everyone reacts to: Minako questions the claim, Mizuki weighs whether he could be lying, Kenji refuses, and Minako and Mizuki then commit. B's short turns read like people talking, and Kenji and Shizue stay recognisably themselves right through to the split vote.

The two transcripts are close in structure and content. In B's Round 3, people refer to each other's findings by name (George: 'though Benjamin mentioned the rising cost of mechanical plant'; Benjamin ties B to the underused hall and D to the unfunded AV reserve), so the comparison builds across speakers. B's close also sounds like a group wrapping up: Toshio notes consensus forming, George concedes, Mizuki just says 'Agreed', and Benjamin remarks on the rare agreement. A has some real moments too, such as Victoria's caveat about the hall being out of service and George holding out for A, but its Round 1 splits into a round of general aims followed by a mechanical round of task assignments. Overall B reads slightly more like an actual exchange.

B's Round 1 is weak, with nearly everyone saying 'I'll stick with my choices' several times over, but its later rounds actually work towards the decision. In B's Round 2, Misaki brings new information (a third of members cannot reach campus early), and Ryuji puts the findings together into a case for the lodge, conditional on the financial risks Mio raised. In Round 3, Mio proposes a strict headcount, Shizue and Ryuji take it up, and Mio changes her vote with a stated reason, which is a believable path to persuasion. A instead loops through the same positions: Misaki and Mio repeat 'fiscally responsible / fair' and Rin repeats 'adventure / grumpy' in every round, and the final round is a deadlock restated three times with no one moved. A also has Misaki claiming exactly the same research items as Mio in Round 1.

B's participants answer each other directly (Shunichi: 'May is already on that, Midori'; 'That's a fair point, Midori, but...'), and Asuka's point about the narrow frontages and driveways creates real tension over whether rotation is workable, which the group has to resolve before agreeing. The concrete details (14 complaints, truck at 7:40, 90 cm of pavement) give later turns something specific to argue over. In A, consensus on rotation forms smoothly by the end of Round 2, and Round 3 is fifteen nearly identical rounds of 'I vote for Option B', which does not read like people talking. A's Round 1 also runs long on filler about the 'fort for trash'.

Both reach Fixed Desks quickly and with similar arguments. In B, people speak from concrete personal concerns (Mizuki on early birds taking the best seats, Shion on printer noise), and Yumi reconciles her collaboration concern with option C by noting it keeps project partners together, which fits who she is. B's wrap-up thins down to single-letter 'C.' turns, which is how a group closes once everyone agrees. A's Round 2 runs the same five positions three times in a generalised way, and Round 3 ends in a formulaic round of 'I'll vote for Fixed Desks by Function to ...' from everyone. A does give Yumi a believable reluctant concession, so the margin is small.

In A the Day 1 discussion turns on a concrete event: Benjamin accuses Shizue, Minako asks him outright whether he is claiming Seer, Mizuki weighs whether he could be the wolf lying, and Kenji pushes back. Those are short, reactive turns that move toward the vote. B's Day 0 is long persona display that ends in a round of ritual goodnights from everyone. B's Day 1 builds a pile-on against Shizue from 'too perfect calmness' and 'symbiotic shield' lines, which read as stylized speeches more than talk. B also breaks consistency at the end: Kenji says he will vote for himself to protect Shizue, then votes Shizue. A is terse and somewhat flat, but its turns respond to one another and its people stay recognisable.

A's Day 1 is driven by Toshio's Seer claim. Jonathan asks 'Are you the Seer?', Mizuki spells out the stakes ('If Kenji is the wolf the game ends today...'), and Kenji protests in character, so the talk converges naturally on the vote. B spends all of Day 0 on strategy platitudes and goodnights. B's Day 1 circles around asking whether the Seer will speak, and then the votes land on Sakura over 'impulsive approach' with little lead-up. Sakura's 'Teehee' becomes a mechanical tic. B's Day 2 has Mizuki reasoning oddly ('then I must be the only one left, but I am a Villager'), and the final turns end without anyone engaging the others' arguments. A's quick exchanges read more like people reacting to each other.

B opens with each person stating what they care about before picking what to check (Ryuji on organizer burnout, Rin on sleep). Their Round 3 positions follow from those concerns and findings: Ryuji wants C to avoid cooking and paperwork, Rin rejects crowded public rooms, Misaki favours B's fixed rates. Round 3 of B also has real back-and-forth: Mio asks 'will people actually come?', Ryuji retorts 'it's also about the organizers' sanity, Mio', and Mio openly changes her vote. Ryuji backs Campus despite having raised the canteen and cooking burden, and Misaki votes Campus right after calling it complicated for commuters. Shizue's 'I'll consider the others' followed by an immediate C vote is also abrupt.

Both end in unanimous B with a repetitive Round 3. B carries more friction and reaction between distinct people: Shunichi needles Rin's 'treasure hunt' and Midori's 'harmony', May tells him not to be a killjoy, and Asuka counters May with 'Simplicity is not a substitute for equity.' In B's Round 3, Midori briefly floats A before coming round, and Asuka keeps adding a real caveat about narrow frontages. In A, the group converges on rotation within Round 2 with near-identical agreement lines. A's Round 3 has every person restating the B vote three times with little new content. B's personalities stay sharper and its discussion does more work toward the decision.

A keeps its turns compact, and Yumi is a real dissenting voice. In Round 2 she says 'we're forgetting how much we gain when we actually talk to each other', and in Round 3 she concedes reluctantly ('if everyone else is this worried about the stress, I'll go with Fixed Desks too'), which reads like a person yielding to a group. B's Round 1 has a long block of 'I'm ready' turns after topics are chosen, and its Round 3 repeats 'I vote for Option C' up to four times per person after consensus is already clear. In B, Yumi's communication concern gets folded into support for fixed desks with no tension, so the decision feels pre-settled. Both converge on C, but A's path reads more like people negotiating.

In B, Day 1 builds around something concrete: Benjamin accuses Shizue, Minako asks him straight out whether he is claiming Seer, Mizuki weighs whether he could be a lying wolf, and Kenji pushes back. The votes then follow what people said: Kenji and Shizue both vote Benjamin, which fits their objections. Kenji says he'll vote for himself to protect Shizue, then votes Shizue, and Shizue votes for herself without comment. A's Day 0 runs long with stiff, speech-like turns and drawn-out goodnights, while B moves at a more conversational pace.

In B, people answer each other directly. On Day 0 Kenji jumps in right after Sakura teases him ('Hey! I'm just excited!'), breaking the speaking order the way a real reply would. On Day 1, Toshio's Seer claim is questioned by Jonathan and Mizuki before people commit. A's Day 1 vote on Sakura arrives with little build-up (Mizuki never says who she is voting for). On Day 2, Mizuki suddenly announces her own role, which reads more like reasoning laid out for the game than a person talking. B's characters stay distinct and brief, and the discussion heads straight to the decision.

Round 3 of A has real back-and-forth. That reads like people working toward a decision. A also opens with each person's goals before they pick what to look into, and Misaki's lone vote for B fits her concern with the budget throughout. B's Round 1 is just a list of picks, and in Round 3 people mostly announce their votes without engaging each other. Shizue says she'll 'consider the others' and then votes C anyway, without any discussion of it.

Both drift into repeated vote announcements in Round 3, so the difference is how they get there. A has more friction between distinct people. May calls Shunichi a 'killjoy' in Round 1, Shunichi needles Midori that harmony is 'a mask', and in Round 2 Asuka keeps pushing that 'Simplicity is not a substitute for equity' against May and Shunichi. In Round 3 Midori first leans toward A before coming round, and Shunichi's 'fair distribution of misery' is picked up by May. B's Round 2 builds neatly toward rotation, but everyone agrees smoothly, and Asuka hands over the conclusion almost like a summary. B's Round 3 is three near-identical rounds of everyone endorsing B with no one disagreeing.

B keeps a dissenting voice: Yumi argues in Round 2 that 'we're focusing so much on the downsides of moving', and in Round 3 says she still feels the social side is being lost before she reluctantly goes along. That makes the agreement feel arrived at rather than automatic. A's Round 1 is padded with a round of 'I'm ready' turns. A's Round 3 turns into a loop: everyone votes C immediately and then restates the vote two or three more times ('The decision is final', 'I stand by my vote'). Turns in B are brief and refer back to each other's points (Shion: 'I'm with Mizuki'), which reads more like a conversation.

In A, Day 1 builds out of what was actually said. Mizuki picks up Shizue's unruffled calm, Kenji defends her, Minako turns that defence back on him, and Mizuki then names the 'loop of mutual protection' once Shizue defends Kenji in return. Each turn answers the one before. B's Day 0 slips into rules-sheet talk (Minako: 'we have a Possessed player who knows the Werewolf's identity'), and after Benjamin's Seer claim on Day 1 the talk keeps repeating 'unless a second Seer appears' until the vote. A has its own flaw: Kenji says he will vote for himself and then votes Shizue, and the case against Shizue rests on little. On the whole, though, A reads more like people reacting to each other.

A moves at a conversational pace with short turns of uneven length: Jonathan's 'That could be anyone in this circle', Kenji's 'No! This is unfair!', and Sakura's teasing of Kenji that he answers right away. On Day 1, Jonathan asks 'Are you the Seer?' and Toshio confirms, which is a natural exchange. B's Kenji also pleads 'just one more day!' and then votes for himself, while A's Kenji consistently votes against his accuser, Toshio.

A is terse, but each line reacts to the last. Jonathan's sudden claim gets Mizuki's immediate counter, Misaki's 'Mizuki is always confident. It's hard to tell', and Rin's naive reasoning, and the talk heads straight to a decision. B's Day 1 has a good stretch: Mizuki presses Jonathan on his vague 'sense of who we might trust' and Misaki joins in. But Day 0 is padded with near-identical 'let us observe' turns and long good-nights. B's Day 2 also falls into confusion, with Misaki saying the attacked Benjamin is 'still alive' and Mizuki quoting 'the rules state...', which breaks the sense of a natural conversation. A's people stay distinct (Benjamin's wry asides, Rin's impulsiveness) without the padding.

In A, each person reports and then restates only their own finding, and Round 3 is five parallel endorsements of rotation ('It is the most logical choice for equality'), with almost no one responding to anyone else. In B, people build on each other: Midori asks 'Is there any way to keep it cheap but still solve the problem?', Shunichi and May follow up ('Exactly. If it's a rotating job...'), and Asuka acknowledges the unfairness to one neighbour while pointing to physical limits. B's Round 3 has people weighing the options against each other, and Asuka stays herself to the end by dissenting for A on the filing burden she investigated. B's concrete figures (over two hundred thousand yen) also make the findings sound like things people actually looked up.

A's Round 3 turns into a loop: everyone restates 'I vote for Option C' three or four times with lines like 'The decision is final', and Round 2 is mostly each person re-saying their priority. B has real friction that drives the talk. Shion dismisses Mizuki's fairness concern ('Fairness is a vague concept', 'Resentment is a byproduct of inefficiency'), and Mizuki keeps pushing to settle the window seats even after the C consensus. Toshio's 'I have no interest in mysteries' in reply to Rin, and his 'Energy is irrelevant', show people answering one another with distinct and stable temperaments. B's post-consensus turns move to the next real question (seat allocation) instead of repeating the vote.

In A, Day 1 settles right after Benjamin's seer claim, and after that Mizuki, Minako and Benjamin keep repeating 'unless a second Seer appears' without adding anything new. In B, Day 1 actually develops: Mizuki questions Shizue's calm, Kenji defends her, Minako turns suspicion onto Kenji's protectiveness, Shizue defends Kenji, and Mizuki points out that the two are covering for each other. Each line builds on the one before. Kenji stays the impulsive, loyal one throughout B, though his last line ('voting for myself') doesn't match the vote he casts. Day 0 in B also reads more naturally, for example Shizue telling Minako not to be stern with 'the young man'.

B is paced like real talk. Lines are short, people skip turns, Sakura jokes about Kenji on Day 0, Kenji fires back 'Hey!', and Mizuki tells Sakura off for joking. Jonathan stays quiet and terse the whole way, and Kenji keeps protesting and then votes for Toshio, which fits everything he said. In A, people deliberate more and Mizuki asks Sakura directly what she thinks, but the turns are uniformly long and polished, and Kenji pleads 'You're making a huge mistake!' and then votes for himself. A's Day 0 also has everyone speak at every chance with similar wrap-up lines.

A plays out like a real exchange. On Day 1 Jonathan hedges, Mizuki and Misaki call his vagueness out, and he gives in and claims seer. Doubt about how convenient the timing is then leads to his execution. On Day 2 Misaki makes a factual slip (that Benjamin is alive), Mizuki corrects her, Misaki apologizes, and the slip becomes grounds for suspicion that Misaki turns back on Mizuki. That kind of mistake-and-repair is very human. B is responsive but sparse: Mizuki is accused and only says 'bold lie' without counter-arguing, and the others pile on with one-liners. Day 0 in B also trails off with Benjamin's 'I shall pass'.

Both transcripts are mostly parallel statements, each person reporting their own findings. A has a bit more back-and-forth: in Round 2 May answers Shunichi with 'Exactly. If it's a rotating job...', and Midori asks the group if anything is cheap but still works. In Round 3 of A, everyone weighs all three options from their own angle, and Asuka holds on to her concern about the filing and votes A. That makes her a distinct person who stays herself. In B, Round 3 ends with a run of one-line echoes ('It prevents one person from feeling targeted', 'It is the most logical choice for equality'). Asuka also drops her paperwork objection with no reason given, which makes it unanimous too easily.

A has real friction that carries through the talk. In Round 2 Shion dismisses Mizuki's fairness as 'a vague concept' and says 'resentment is a byproduct of inefficiency', and Toshio replies 'Energy is irrelevant' to Rin. After everyone backs C in Round 3, Mizuki keeps pushing to settle who gets the window and interior-wall seats while Shion argues for priority by productivity, so the group moves on to the next practical issue. In B, nearly every turn agrees with the last, and Round 3 turns into a dozen repeats of 'I vote for Option C' with no new content, which reads mechanical. Personas show up in both, but A lets them clash.

In A, Day 1 settles on a single path the moment Benjamin claims Seer: Mizuki, Minako and Benjamin keep repeating 'unless a second Seer appears, the evidence is conclusive', with nobody pushing back, and Shizue ends up voting for herself, which no real person would do. In B, Day 1 has no claim, so people have to work under uncertainty. Mizuki picks up Benjamin's 'strategic risk' remark and the 'dance' wording, Minako asks him directly, Benjamin parries in character and Kenji objects that it's too hasty. On Day 2 of B the survivors react to the deaths, and Mizuki narrows it to Shizue or Kenji while Kenji turns her detective act against her. That exchange builds turn by turn. The personalities in B also stay recognisable without the formulaic restating seen in A.

Both follow the same arc: Toshio claims Kenji is the wolf and the group goes along. A's utterance lengths vary naturally. Jonathan's reserved one-liners on Day 0 ('It is simply my nature') read like a real quiet person answering Mizuki's probe, and on Day 1 Mizuki hands the floor to the hesitant Sakura. B makes every turn about the same length, Sakura's 'Hehe' tic gets mechanical, and on Day 0 Kenji answers 'I'm not trying to deflect anything, Sakura!' to an accusation that Toshio actually aimed at Sakura, which is a misattributed reply. A's self-vote by Kenji is a flaw, but B's Day 1 is mostly long restatements of the same risk-reward argument. On balance A's pacing feels more like talk.

A is terse to the point of being skeletal. Day 0 is a handful of slogans and a 'pass', and on Day 1 the reasoning stays thin: Rin's 'He's too quiet to be a mean wolf' carries no argument, and the others simply follow. In B, people build on each other. On Day 0 Rin reads Mizuki's remark as defending her, and Misaki points out that a confirmed human becomes a target. On Day 1 Mizuki argues that she is being framed because she is logical, Rin turns that around and then echoes Mizuki's point about the Seer exposing himself, Misaki counters with efficiency, and Benjamin weighs the two performances. The movement to the vote in B is visible and argued, and the speakers keep distinct voices.

A is brisk but oddly frictionless and sometimes incoherent. In Round 3 Midori says B seems well supported and then agrees with A, Servas leans 'A or C' and votes A, and Benjamin calls A's 'simulation and data aspects' robust even though he had flagged field risk, so everyone ends up on A without an exchange that explains it. B's first two rounds are padded with platitudes from Servas and Midori, but Round 3 holds a real disagreement. Servas, Midori and Benjamin back B, Kenji objects that the glasshouses are booked solid, Toshio presses the case for a catalogue, and Servas and then Midori shift with stated reasons, while Benjamin concedes reluctantly. That sequence reads like people persuading each other towards the decision.

The two are similar in content, but A's Round 2 is mostly parallel statements of each person's own concern with little engagement. A's Round 3 also collapses into everyone saying 'C' with no one holding out. In B, people react to each other in Round 2: Mizuki's 'But if we stay fixed, some people are stuck with the worst spots forever' pushes back on Toshio, Rin gradually moves to 'stability is better than flexibility', and Yumi proposes grouping by function as a bridge. In B's Round 3 Mizuki still weighs Rotating Blocks for fairness and then explicitly concedes to the group, which is a believable path to a consensus.

In A, Day 1 builds up naturally: Minako presses Benjamin about his 'strategic risk' remark, Mizuki brings up his 'dance' wording from Day 0, and Kenji reacts to how tense it is getting, so the suspicion grows out of what was actually said. Day 2 of A is a clear three-way confrontation, and Kenji turns Mizuki's detective stance back on her in character. In B, once Benjamin claims Seer on Day 1, nobody challenges the claim or asks whether it could be fake, even though Benjamin himself raised that possibility on Day 0. Mizuki and Minako also repeat 'unless a second Seer appears' several times without moving anything forward. B also ends with Shizue voting for herself right after pleading that she is innocent, which no real person would do.

The two follow the same course, but B's turns vary more in length and feel more like talk. On Day 0 of B, Jonathan is quiet and gives short answers that fit him, Mizuki asks him directly why he is so reserved, and he answers briefly. On Day 1, Mizuki turns to Sakura ('you seem hesitant; what do you think?'), which moves the decision along like a facilitator would. A has a misdirected reply on Day 0: Kenji says 'I'm not trying to deflect anything, Sakura!' when it was Toshio that Sakura had needled. Also in A, Toshio says 'I will use tonight's divination' before he has claimed Seer, and on Day 1 several speakers recite the same 'if he's lying he's committing suicide' logic. B has its own flaw, Kenji voting for himself, but its conversation flows better overall.

On Day 1 of A, the argument develops step by step. Mizuki asks why a real Seer would reveal himself so early, Rin picks this up ('Please eat me tonight!'), Misaki answers it with the efficiency argument, and Benjamin compares the two 'performances'. Each turn responds to the one before and moves the group toward its decision. On Day 0 of A, Misaki's warning that a confirmed human becomes a target is also a real reply to what Rin said. B's quick exchanges sound conversational in places (Misaki's 'Or someone who is too quiet', 'Mizuki is always confident'). But Jonathan and Mizuki mostly restate their positions, so the shift toward Jonathan is barely worked through. A's turns are long and a bit speech-like, but the participants are clearly reasoning their way to the vote.

Rounds 1 and 2 of A are padded with ceremonial filler: in Round 1 everyone announces they are 'retiring to quiet reflection' while waiting for data, and in Round 2 there are three cycles of near-identical remarks about balance and pragmatism. Few real people talk like that. A's Round 3 does have a real persuasion arc, with Kenji pointing out the glasshouses are fully booked, Servas and Midori changing sides, and Benjamin holding out before conceding. B is a working meeting: in Round 2 each person reports a finding, then they draw implications from it ('shouldn't pick something that needs that broken spectroscopy machine'). In Round 3, Servas weighs field work against technician scarcity and Midori goes back and forth between A and B. B has rough spots, such as Midori listing out the candidates and Servas's thin reason for switching, but its pace reads much more like people doing a task together.

Both are short and businesslike, but A shows positions changing in response to each other. Mizuki's 'But if we stay fixed, some people are stuck with the worst spots forever' pushes back on Rin and Toshio. Rin says she is 'starting to think stability is better'. In Round 3, Mizuki concedes openly ('If the rest of you feel this strongly... I'll concede'), and Shion follows with a dry 'Finally'. B has more concrete detail (the printer noise, window seats, people arriving at eight). But its Round 3 opening is five parallel speeches that each knock out the same options in turn, and Shion's 'Exactly' replies to a fairness point about arrival times rather than to his own concern. So B reads more like statements placed side by side, and A more like people reaching a decision together.

In A on Day 1, Benjamin only says he has 'interesting information' and never actually claims Seer, yet Minako and Mizuki react as if he had, and Mizuki's 'his information is absolute' is a stock line. Many of A's lines are generic filler ('I think we should just listen to each other and be kind') that don't pick up on the previous speaker. In B, Minako directly asks Shizue to answer the accusation, Mizuki questions Kenji's emotional defence and asks Benjamin why he revealed early, and Benjamin gives an answer, so the questions and answers build on each other. B's Kenji also has a believable arc, resisting and then reluctantly going with the group, while A's Kenji just repeats 'she's too sweet'. B has some polished, literary phrasing, but it reads more like people pushing toward a decision.

B's Day 0 already has real friction: Mizuki picks up Kenji's 'honest' remark, Toshio questions why Mizuki is focusing on Kenji, Sakura turns it back on Toshio, and each one answers. B's Day 1 is a back-and-forth on Toshio's claim in which Mizuki asks Kenji to respond, Sakura questions Mizuki's lean, and the votes follow from what was argued.
